name: Santa Fe Depot

dates.note: Wikipedia's infobox prints 'Built 1915'; the city's archive page dates the opening to March 8, 1915 and a Santa Fe centenary post to March 7, 1915. The one-day disagreement is recorded and neither date is adopted.

refs.title: NRHP reference No. 72000248; added to the National Register 26 June 1972; area 4.6 acres; architect Bakewell and Brown; architectural style 'Mission/Spanish Revival' (as the Wikipedia infobox prints it)
San Diego Historic Landmark No. 56, designated 4 February 1972 (a city designation, not a state register file)
San Diego, CA – Santa Fe Depot (SAN) – Great American Stations
refs.note: 'Constructed to welcome the world to the 1915 Panama-California Exposition, the Santa Fe Depot is a city landmark known for its soaring towers and tiled domes', built by the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe from 1914-1915.

refs.title: Opening Day of the Santa Fe Depot in 1915

note: Seeded 5 Sep 2026. No HABS survey found and none asserted. Worth carrying for the node: the Wikipedia infobox files the building under 'Mission/Spanish Revival', a compound the National Register uses for both of this cluster's revival styles at once, so the depot's assignment to `mission-revival` rests on the architecture (twin domed towers over an arcaded front) and not on the register's label.
